newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan cuts fodder prices for livestock owners.
newsitem.headline: Jordan cuts fodder prices for livestock owners.

text.p: Jordan reduced on Saturday by 7.5 percent the price of animal fodder sold to the country's livestock owners, the state news agency said.

Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti was quoted as saying the price cut was to make good a government pledge to reduce -- when world grain prices dropped -- the prices of basic commodities it imports.
These commodities, including wheat and sugar, are then resold to retailers and citizens.
The price of one tonne of yellow corn, effective December 1, will be reduced to a fixed 148 dinars ($211) from 160 dinars set after a 33 percent price hike last August.
Many pastoral Jordanians are nomadic Bedouins for whom livestock rearing is the main source of income.
World grain prices have fallen substantially since reaching record highs in the first half of the year.

Jordan, worried about a worsening budget deficit from a higher food import bill, took the decision last August on advice from the International Monetary Fund to virtually double bread prices and animal fodder overnight.
The price hikes sparked widespread unrest.

Kabariti, who was speaking after a visit to the ministry of supply, said the state was ready to end importing basic commodities if the private sector could prove it was capable of supplying the local market "with sufficient quantities at reasonable prices."
